title: The Corruption of Praise and the Nature of Wisdom
english: It is as if he has nothing; for he who loves silver will never be satisfied with silver. Or indeed, the faithful person will see the words of this world as if they were spoken metaphorically as matters of the mind; but the unfaithful person will not even touch the words of a chance matter because of the impurity of the soul.
Stanza 26. Regarding one who hides his own ignorance or his passion by silence, it seems to be near.

Stanza 27. He does not carry out all evil (for it is impossible), but performs those things capable of co-existing; and even while doing evil, he did not cease. Or he speaks of Christ as a good concept; for He himself guarantees it; and everyone doing good things will find Him; for he speaks of the one doing every good work as prudent.

Stanza 24. He who does not live rightly hides the hands unjustly in the soul; not wishing to work his own land, how shall he be filled with bread? For the practical virtues have a connection to the hands, bringing our bread to the mouth which has come down from heaven (Matt 6:11). Therefore, this one, being slothful, cannot even benefit from the beginning.
Stanza 10. For indeed the judgment covers the defense of the ungodly. For God exceeds those doing good in rewards.
Stanza 16. Do not give yourself over to being too ashamed to repent. For if you die and do not have time to repent, you will no longer have rest.

Stanza 23. And he who acts with vainglory or human-pleasing in doing something of the good works brings the devil, the snare, in with him, and eats his own morsel with him; for such a one withholds his own reward. And indeed the devil...

He offers these things to men, so that through the praise of the man-pleaser he may be defiled and be deprived of the eternal goods. Verse 4. Evil men will not produce virtues and right doctrines (for these are the offspring of the soul), because they do not fear the Lord; but those being in the fear of the Lord will have offspring all their days, and their hope will not be removed (Psalm 128:3). And these things follow what was said. For the enemies, he says, being evil, find advantage in the falls of others; but that which you reproach, do not envy. For their bright thing is bound and deceptive, until this life, and it is extinguished at the end; and often even while living it was exposed and was extinguished.

Verse 7. The wise man says these things by wisdom, or the slave of Christ to the Lord. And having said two, he asks concerning more; but what seems to be first is a prerequisite to the chance of obtaining what he asks, saying: Do not pass me by, but give grace; whereupon the first brought a request: Do not make my word a vain, long-winded falsehood, so that, not being filled, I may become a liar. The boy makes pride, and the appearance of being [wise] to be instead of an examination; by word and deed as if without sin. For the [phrase], 'Who sees me?', instead of 'Reprove me', he says; so that, not being filled with wisdom, he may be incomprehensible in glory to others, or even appear a liar speaking concerning these things.

Verse 15. The leech is born indeed in the sweet waters, being a worm-like creature; and it is most smooth to the touch, which, taking hold of the grain of the water, enters unnoticed by its smoothness; then, having entwined itself within some...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Devil's Methods and the Soul's Flight
english: The veins of the body are not ruptured before the shedding of blood kills the man; for it is a blood-drinker, and from this it is nourished and grows. In this way he now resembles the parasite. He is the one who is unable to rule by the force of men; for he has made use of three main impulses against them: pleasure, seduction, and deception, and because of this, having undermined them little by little, he overthrows them. First, indeed, he leads them into the paths of false doctrine toward destruction, which is indeed called 'sweetness,' showing the magnitude of sin at its end; then, surrounding them with the pleasure of lawlessness, which is indeed called the lust for women. Upon these is added love of money, that is, greed, which he said does not even fill the earth with water; for such is the sandy, insatiable thing. These, then, are the passions which the evil one has discovered for the destruction of men, whom he loves and cherishes as if they were his own daughters.

The fourth [method] he calls the friction and habit of these; for not even one who has falsely believed, or committed fornication, or desired more, immediately fell into these passions, but having been defeated in the remainder by habit and sensation; for such people you would find buried in false doctrines, never receiving a child, but always promoting the passions, as well as inciting others to these things. Just as indeed neither water nor fire ceases at the supply of what is being poured out, nor does it say, 'It is enough,' but rather it becomes an overflowing; the water, by the pouring in of water, does not stop, but increases; which also you, he says, O child, knowing, should abstain from, so that you may not be lost in a short time, like the finest thief, plundering life through pleasure.

The tracks of a soaring eagle are the soul of the wise, which, being wise, is unable to know from itself the flights of the intellectual eagle; about which it is written: 'The great eagle and he who has long wings and is full of claws' (Job 39:26), not having a trace of the presence of the devil, although I did not know from where he flew before me; for the evil one departing from me, I did not know, because I did not have desire toward him. Such is the path of the harlot, the corrupted teaching.

The people from the Gentiles, being formerly a slave to sin and to the devil; thus: 'I greatly vex you with my fury' (Gal 5:20); and, 'O foolish one, filled with the foods of life' (Prov 9:2); and, 'Harlot woman,' which is a prostitute; for the Church from the Gentiles was a prostitute, walking after foreign gods; and a maidservant who casts out her own mistress, the Church of the Gentiles being the Synagogue as mistress; for of this, the law and the prophets are required. The literal investigation is a slave to the intellectual contemplation, which the Jews preferred as a mistress; but the Gentiles, receiving the literal as the spiritual, cast off the physical observance of the law as a mistress among them. He says the Gentiles, who have no strength, and treasure for themselves eternal life through good works. And the pig-rollers; a kind of fish, that is, the so-called hares, the oysters, the former...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Proverbial Exegesis
english: Weak nations fleeing to Christ; for a rock is a refuge for swine who made [dwellings] in rocks. And you, he says, even if you are a weak animal, take hold of the rock of true faith, and direct your life toward it. One entering the kingdom is said to be relying on a deed.

Surely you, he says, do not through weakness of faith become unbelieving toward the kingdom of the heavens, but believing in the promise concerning it, participate in the precepts of this that are doing [the work]. Lion Christ; for all rational things are cattle to him; for Moses says, 'But I am irrational' (Exodus 4:10). It is said to pass through natural energy without hindrance.

[St. 40] He who is drawn toward sins, and walking in loftiness, has the flock clinging to him. 'For when I am exalted,' he says, 'I will draw all things toward myself.' The rooster bears the face of the teacher, who strongly proclaims the light, sowing the word in the souls. 'Repent; for the kingdom of heaven has come near' (Matthew 4:17). This was he who from the beginning was piercing the hearts of men, and through many was foretelling the day of his incarnate presence; and driving out darkness, and clearly showing the eternal light to all. Walking among females [churches] cheerfully, that is, in the Churches, cheerfully and bravely, as he says, 'Behold, I am with you all the days until the completion of the age' (Matthew 28:20).

[St. 42] Or if you bring yourself into the mind of the Scriptures; or, if you do not have a student's ear, but are argumentative, do you hear? 'And if you are a man of contention, we do not have such a habit.' [St. 3] Do not give your wealth to strange pleasures or teachings. To drink wine with intention. He who drinks the wine of the true vine, the interpretation of the Scriptures, and the contemplation of existing things, with much approaching discernment of the intellect's oversight.

[St. 6] Now he called pain 'toil.' Therefore those who toil and suffer for God, even if they become intoxicated with the drink of the Lord's house, forget the pains. [St. 7] Have your will toward attending to my words, spoken by God. [St. 23] The North Wind, the devil, stirring up and tempting the saints who are lofty, and not wanting to work; or stirring up words against his own dogmas. [St. 3] Just as these things are rather transferred to the benefit of animals, so the rod, that is, rebuke, regulates the lawless nation.

[St. 7] Of such things, he says, he rather strips away the power, and neither pours out a practical principle nor a rational one to these. [St. 14] If a tree of life is nourished from fruits of righteousness, everyone hiding righteousness with injustice, which is called a hand, will not eat from the tree of life. [St. 23] Of your disciples, so that you do not lead the teaching toward outward appearance. [St. 22] He says that the contemplation of events, and the contemplation of the Holy Trinity, is a garment for a pure mind, of fine linen and purple (Revelation 19:8).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
